subject: LendWell pilot: model-fit evaluation & sample prompt collection
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@lendwellfinance.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@lendwellfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: LendWell discovery recap + next steps (pilot sample prompts)

Alexis / Jordan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope a pilot that validates model fit and surface potential quality regressions before a larger rollout.

Summary of needs you shared:
- Customer support triage + AHT reduction (high priority)
- Regulatory-safe summarization for loan decision notes (PII sensitive)
- High variance in historical prompt phrasing (lots of edge cases)

Suggested pilot scope (30-day):
- Ingest a ~10k sample set of real user prompts (we only need text, you can redact names/account numbers)
- Run model-fit evals across 2 model families: compact (fast/cheap) + standard (higher f1/quality)
- Evaluate on: accuracy of intent classification, hallucination rate on fact queries, and summary fidelity for decision notes

Immediate asks (can you action these?):
1) Fill the attached prompt_collection_template.csv with 200–500 representative queries (mix of short, long, and multi-turn). Flag any prompts you consider "high-risk" (PII, legal language, financial identifiers).
2) Share 2–3 labeled edge cases where current automation fails.
3) Confirm whether procurement needs an initial SOW or PO to proceed.

What we will provide:
- Pilot eval plan (attached -> pilot_eval_plan_v1.pdf) with recommended metrics and acceptance criteria
- Redaction guidance doc (data_redaction_guidelines.md) and a simple client-side redaction checklist
- Initial model recommendations and benchmarks (see next email)

Timeline we’re aiming for: template returned by 2028-07-18, pilot kick-off the week of 2028-07-25. If that works, I’ll loop in our solutions engineer to start the ingest workflow.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0133

From: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@lendwellfinance.com>

Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@lendwellfinance.com>, procurement <procurement@lendwellfinance.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LendWell discovery recap + next steps (pilot sample prompts)

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. Team confirmed we can produce the sample set but need more detail on PII redaction expectations. A couple quick clarifications: 

- For redaction, do you accept token-level masking or do you require full replace-with-[REDACTED]? We need to understand if internal IDs should be preserved (hashed) for analytics.
- On the models: are you recommending any quantized runtimes that preserve hallucination characteristics? Cost will be a gating factor for us.

I pasted two short example prompts that illustrate our variability (we’ll fill the CSV next week):
1) "Customer says they didn't get the payment confirmation but card charged — what should I do?"
2) "Borrower income seems inconsistent across docs — summarize differences and highlight missing pieces for underwriter."

Also adding procurement on the thread. Procurement asked if you can share a simple SOW template or if you prefer DocuSign pilot agreement.

Best — Alexis

On Tue, Jul 11, 2028 at 10:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Alexis / Jordan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope a pilot...

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@lendwellfinance.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@lendwellfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LendWell discovery recap + next steps (pilot sample prompts)

Thanks Alexis — quick answers inline and a consolidated ask so procurement can review.

Redaction: we accept either approach but recommend client-side deterministic hashing for internal IDs and full token replacement (e.g., [REDACTED_NAME], [REDACTED_ACCT]) for PII categories that must be omitted from model inputs. The attached data_redaction_guidelines.md has a short checklist. If you prefer, we can ship a tiny client-side filter script to run before upload.

Quantized runtimes and model recommendations (initial):
- Fast/cheap baseline: a 4–6B quantized variant (we recommend trying redwood/open-6b-int8 first) — good throughput, lower cost, decent intent classification
- Higher-quality baseline: a 13B family with mixed precision (redwood/open-13b-fp16) — better summarization fidelity, lower hallucination rate on fact-based items
- If you want to test a production-grade low-latency variant we can run a 13B quantized + KV-cache config during the pilot for the summary pathway.

Benchmarks & evals:
- We’ll run intent classification accuracy, hallucination sampling against a curated factset, and summary ROUGE/F1-style fidelity checks. I’ve uploaded the draft eval notebook and baseline metrics to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LendWellPilot (see file: lendwell_baseline_metrics.ipynb)

Procurement / SOW: we can do a simple DocuSign pilot agreement to speed things up — sharing a link below. If procurement insists on a PO first, we can accept it too; we’ll need a signed pilot agreement before any paid capacity is provisioned.

Ask: Please return the populated prompt_collection_template.csv and flag 20 high-risk edge cases by 2028-07-18 so we can lock the pilot scope. If timelines slip, tell us your preferred timing and we’ll adapt.

cc: Ben and Marissa — can you validate the metric set below and confirm we’re OK to propose the two-model family approach?

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: LendWell pilot - metric tweak suggestion

Quick internal note — reading the examples Alexis provided, I recommend we: 
- Add an "information recall" check for the summarization task (does the summary preserve loan-relevant numeric facts?)
- Include a prompt-sensitivity slice (short vs long prompts) since they called out multi-turn variability
- Limit initial expensive runs to a 1k subset (stratified by intent and length) to keep pilot costs predictable, then expand if acceptance thresholds met

Also suggest we propose an optional anti-regression gating: if hallucination rate rises >3% versus baseline, flag for model rollback. I'll add this to the pilot_eval_plan_v1.pdf before sharing externally.

Ben
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
